baslik: The Hurricane That Pushed a Lake Over Its Dike
sonuc: overflowed and drowned farm towns
tetik: hurricane winds piling lake water against a low dike
mekanizma: wind-driven surge on a shallow lake overtopping and breaching a small earthen dike
ders: the Herbert Hoover Dike was built around the lake
yanilgi: The deadly water didn't come from the ocean. The hurricane pushed Lake Okeechobee itself over its banks.
tartisma: Most victims were migrant farm workers. Who does infrastructure protect first?
basliklar: Why the 1928 Okeechobee Hurricane Was So Deadly
The Lake That Became a Storm Surge
sahneler: A hurricane drove Lake Okeechobee over its dike.
Within hours, floodwater swept through farm towns, and thousands were killed.
The water didn't come from the ocean.
Hurricane winds piled the shallow lake against its southern shore.
The dike there was low and made of earth.
It was overtopped and broke.
Most victims were migrant farm workers.
The massive Herbert Hoover Dike was built afterward.

baslik: The Reservoir That Overfilled Because Its Sensors Came Loose
sonuc: overflowed and breached its wall
tetik: water level sensors that had come loose
mekanizma: pumping continued past full because level sensors read low, overtopping and eroding the embankment
ders: the reservoir was rebuilt with independent overfill protection
yanilgi: The pumps weren't broken. They kept filling because the sensors said the reservoir wasn't full.
tartisma: A backup sensor had been set too high. How independent must a backup be?
basliklar: Why the Taum Sauk Reservoir Breached
The Sensors That Said It Wasn't Full
sahneler: Before dawn, a mountaintop reservoir in Missouri burst its wall.
Within minutes, a billion gallons of water rushed down the mountain.
Pumps had kept filling it past full.
Its water level sensors had come loose.
They reported a lower level than the real one.
A backup sensor was set too high to help.
Water spilled over the wall and eroded it.
The rebuilt reservoir has independent overfill protection.

baslik: The New Dam That Burst on Its First Filling
sonuc: burst as its reservoir filled for the first time
tetik: a crack found hours before the failure
mekanizma: embankment failure likely linked to its clay core and construction on first filling
ders: the flood influenced British reservoir safety legislation
yanilgi: The crack was spotted hours earlier. It was judged not to be urgent.
tartisma: The flood led to huge compensation claims. How do you value what a flood destroys?
basliklar: Why the Dale Dyke Dam Burst
The Great Sheffield Flood
sahneler: A brand-new dam above Sheffield burst at night.
The flood swept through the valley, killing about two hundred forty people.
The reservoir was filling for the first time.
Hours earlier, a worker spotted a crack in the embankment.
It was judged not to be urgent.
Water broke through and tore the dam open.
It was one of Britain's worst dam disasters.
It influenced later reservoir safety laws in Britain.

baslik: The Car Whose Fuel Tank Burst in Rear-End Crashes
sonuc: caught fire in some rear-end collisions
tetik: a fuel tank placed behind the rear axle
mekanizma: fuel tank puncture and filler-neck failure in rear impacts, releasing fuel
ders: Ford recalled the car and US rear-impact fuel system standards were enforced
yanilgi: The Pinto's safety record overall was debated. The specific rear-impact fuel leak problem is what drove the recall.
tartisma: A cost-benefit memo became infamous. Should safety ever be priced in dollars per life?
basliklar: Why the Ford Pinto's Fuel Tank Became Infamous
The Rear-End Crash Problem
hook: The tank was behind the axle
sahneler: In some rear-end crashes, Ford Pinto cars burst into flames.
Several drivers and passengers were killed.
The fuel tank sat behind the rear axle.
In a collision, it could be pushed into sharp parts.
The tank or its filler neck could split and leak fuel.
A spark then ignited it.
The case became a landmark in product liability.
Ford recalled the car to reinforce the fuel system.

baslik: The Car That Helped Create Federal Auto Safety Law
sonuc: became the centre of a national safety debate
tetik: swing-axle rear suspension prone to oversteer
mekanizma: swing-axle geometry causing rear wheel tuck and oversteer when tyre pressures were wrong
ders: the US created federal auto safety standards and an agency to enforce them
yanilgi: Later government testing found the 1960–63 Corvair no worse than rivals. But the debate changed car safety law.
tartisma: A single book turned car safety into politics. Can public pressure drive better engineering?
basliklar: Why the Chevrolet Corvair Became a Safety Scandal
The Swing Axle Behind 'Unsafe at Any Speed'
sahneler: A compact car became the focus of America's first great car safety fight.
Crashes blamed on sudden oversteer led to lawsuits and a best-selling book.
The early Corvair used swing-axle rear suspension.
In hard turns, a rear wheel could tuck under.
Tyre pressures had to be kept exactly right.
Later tests found it no worse than rivals.
But the debate changed the law.
The US created federal auto safety standards soon after.

baslik: The Flood That Proved Levees Alone Couldn't Hold the Mississippi
sonuc: broke in many places and flooded the valley
tetik: months of rain raising the river beyond its levees
mekanizma: a levees-only strategy that confined the river until levees breached
ders: the Flood Control Act of 1928 added spillways and floodways
yanilgi: Higher levees made the river rise higher between them. Engineers needed places to let the water spread.
tartisma: A levee was deliberately dynamited to protect New Orleans. Who decides which land floods?
basliklar: Why the 1927 Mississippi Flood Was So Destructive
The Levees-Only Policy That Failed
sahneler: The Mississippi River broke through its levees in dozens of places.
Floodwater spread across a vast area, and hundreds of thousands were forced from home.
Engineers had relied on levees alone.
Confining the river made it rise higher between them.
Months of heavy rain pushed it past its limits.
A levee was even blown up to protect New Orleans.
The disaster changed river engineering.
The Flood Control Act of 1928 added spillways and floodways.

baslik: The Winter Flood That Put Cities Under Water
sonuc: submerged large parts of river cities
tetik: record January rainfall on frozen ground
mekanizma: extreme runoff overwhelming unprotected riverfront cities
ders: the US built floodwalls and reservoirs along the Ohio River
yanilgi: It wasn't spring snowmelt. It was an unusually wet January on saturated, frozen ground.
tartisma: Floodwalls now protect many cities. Do they encourage building in risky places?
basliklar: Why the 1937 Ohio River Flood Was So Severe
The January Flood That Drowned River Cities
sahneler: In January, the Ohio River rose to record heights.
Floodwater swept through Louisville, Cincinnati and other cities, leaving huge numbers homeless.
Heavy rain fell for weeks.
Frozen and saturated ground couldn't absorb it.
The river kept rising.
Fires broke out and power failed in flooded cities.
The destruction changed flood policy.
Floodwalls and reservoirs were built along the Ohio River.

baslik: The Hurricane That Exposed Poorly Built Homes
sonuc: destroyed tens of thousands of homes in south Florida
tetik: extreme winds on houses with weak roof connections
mekanizma: roof uplift and failure where construction and code enforcement fell short
ders: Florida created a statewide building code with stronger wind rules
yanilgi: Winds alone didn't explain the damage. Poor construction and weak inspections made it far worse.
tartisma: Codes existed but weren't always enforced. Is a code without inspection a code at all?
basliklar: Why Hurricane Andrew Destroyed So Many Homes
The Weak Roofs Hurricane Andrew Exposed
sahneler: Hurricane Andrew smashed into south Florida.
Tens of thousands of homes were destroyed in a single night.
Investigators studied why so many failed.
Many roofs were poorly nailed and weakly connected.
Wind peeled them off.
Broken windows let pressure build inside.
Building codes had not always been enforced.
Florida then created a stronger statewide building code.

baslik: The Unforecast Hurricane That Surprised New England
sonuc: struck New England with little warning
tetik: a fast-moving hurricane forecast to stay out at sea
mekanizma: a rapid-moving storm with a large surge hitting an unprepared coast
ders: hurricane barriers were later built to protect Providence and other harbors
yanilgi: The storm wasn't unknown. Forecasters expected it to curve out to sea.
tartisma: One junior forecaster reportedly argued it would hit land. How should dissenting forecasts be treated?
basliklar: Why the 1938 Hurricane Caught New England Off Guard
The Hurricane Forecast to Turn Away
sahneler: A powerful hurricane slammed into Long Island and New England.
Storm surge swept away homes, and hundreds were killed.
Forecasters expected it to curve out to sea.
Instead, it raced north.
It arrived at high tide.
Downtown Providence flooded deeply.
Many people had no warning at all.
Hurricane barriers were later built to protect Providence.

baslik: Why So Many Buildings Collapsed in the 1999 İzmit Earthquake
sonuc: collapsed many apartment buildings
tetik: strong shaking on poorly built reinforced concrete buildings
mekanizma: soft-storey failures and poor concrete and detailing in reinforced concrete frames
ders: Turkey introduced compulsory earthquake insurance and tightened building inspection
yanilgi: Many collapsed buildings could have survived if built to the code of the time.
tartisma: Codes existed, but enforcement was weak. How do you enforce building quality at scale?
basliklar: Why Buildings Collapsed in the İzmit Earthquake
The Construction Quality an Earthquake Exposed
sahneler: A powerful earthquake struck northwest Turkey before dawn.
Thousands of buildings collapsed, and about seventeen thousand people died.
Many were concrete apartment blocks.
Their ground floors were often open shops with few walls.
Concrete quality and steel detailing were frequently poor.
Codes existed but were weakly enforced.
Floors pancaked onto each other.
Turkey then introduced compulsory earthquake insurance and tighter inspections.

baslik: Why a Moderate Earthquake Was So Deadly in Haiti
sonuc: collapsed buildings across Port-au-Prince
tetik: a shallow quake close to a dense city
mekanizma: collapse of unreinforced and poorly reinforced masonry and concrete without seismic design
ders: Haiti adopted a national building code after the quake
yanilgi: Magnitude alone didn't decide the toll. Building quality and closeness to the city did.
tartisma: Earthquake-resistant building costs money poorer countries may lack. Who should pay for safer buildings?
basliklar: Why the 2010 Haiti Earthquake Was So Deadly
The Buildings That Weren't Designed for Earthquakes
sahneler: A shallow earthquake struck near Haiti's capital.
Buildings collapsed across Port-au-Prince, killing a vast number of people.
The quake was strong but not extreme.
It struck close to a dense city.
Most buildings had no seismic design.
Heavy, brittle concrete and masonry crumbled.
Even government buildings fell.
Haiti adopted a national building code afterward.

baslik: A Volcano and a Typhoon Collapsed Roofs With Wet Ash
sonuc: buried the region in heavy wet ash
tetik: a typhoon soaking the falling ash
mekanizma: rain-saturated ash overloading roofs that collapsed
ders: the forecast-driven evacuation became a model for volcano response
yanilgi: Many deaths weren't from the eruption directly. Roofs collapsed under ash made heavy by rain.
tartisma: Evacuations saved thousands of lives. How do scientists convince people to leave in time?
basliklar: Why Pinatubo's Ash Collapsed So Many Roofs
The Volcano and the Typhoon
soru: How do you get people to leave?
sahneler: Mount Pinatubo erupted in the Philippines.
Within hours, a typhoon swept in over the falling ash.
Rain soaked the falling ash.
Wet ash is far heavier than dry ash.
Roofs across the region collapsed under the weight.
Many of the deaths came from those collapses.
Scientists had forecast the eruption and urged evacuation.
It became a model for volcano response.

baslik: Why One Icelandic Volcano Grounded Europe's Flights
sonuc: shut down much of Europe's airspace
tetik: fine volcanic ash blown toward Europe
mekanizma: ash melting in jet engines at high temperature and fusing onto turbine parts
ders: regulators set ash concentration limits instead of zero tolerance
yanilgi: The ash wasn't just smoke. It is glassy rock that melts inside jet engines.
tartisma: Airlines argued the closures were too cautious. How much uncertainty justifies a shutdown?
basliklar: Why Eyjafjallajökull Grounded European Flights
The Ash That Melts Inside Jet Engines
sahneler: A volcano in Iceland erupted beneath a glacier.
Within days, most of Europe's airspace was closed.
Its ash was fine and glassy.
Winds carried it toward Europe.
Inside a jet engine, that ash can melt.
It can fuse onto turbine parts and stop the engine.
Airlines argued the closures were too cautious.
Regulators then set ash concentration limits for flying.

baslik: The Tornado That Hit a Hospital Head-On
sonuc: tore through Joplin, including its hospital
tetik: an extremely violent tornado crossing the city
mekanizma: windows and exterior failing, letting wind and debris inside the building
ders: new hospitals in tornado areas were designed with safe rooms and hardened walls
yanilgi: The hospital's structure stood. Its windows and exterior failed, and the inside was wrecked.
tartisma: The rebuilt hospital was designed to resist tornadoes. Should all critical buildings be?
basliklar: What the Joplin Tornado Did to a Hospital
The Tornado That Hit St. John's
sahneler: A violent EF5 tornado tore through Joplin, Missouri.
It destroyed thousands of buildings and killed more than one hundred fifty people.
It struck a hospital head-on.
Windows blew in and debris swept through the floors.
Backup generators failed.
Staff carried patients down stairs by hand.
The building had to be demolished.
Its replacement was designed to withstand tornadoes.

baslik: Schools in Tornado Alley Without Storm Shelters
sonuc: destroyed two elementary schools
tetik: an EF5 tornado on a school day
mekanizma: collapse of school buildings without reinforced storm shelters
ders: Moore required storm shelters or safe rooms in new schools and homes
yanilgi: Hallways and interior rooms weren't enough. Only reinforced shelters resist a direct EF5 hit.
tartisma: Shelters cost money for every school. What is the price of a safe room?
basliklar: Why the Moore Tornado Destroyed Schools
The Schools Without Storm Shelters
soru: What is a safe room worth?
sahneler: An EF5 tornado struck Moore, Oklahoma, during the school day.
Two schools were destroyed, and seven children were killed at one of them.
Neither school had a storm shelter.
Children sheltered in hallways and bathrooms.
The tornado collapsed walls and roofs.
Only reinforced safe rooms resist a direct hit like that.
Moore then changed its rules.
New schools and homes now need storm shelters.

baslik: The Bay Bridge Deck That Fell in the 1989 Earthquake
sonuc: dropped a section onto the deck below
tetik: earthquake motion shearing the bolts holding a span
mekanizma: failure of connections at a pier where the span slid off its support
ders: the eastern span was replaced by a new seismically designed bridge
yanilgi: The bridge didn't collapse. One section of the upper deck fell onto the lower deck.
tartisma: The new eastern span took decades and billions to build. How fast should seismic upgrades happen?
basliklar: What Happened to the Bay Bridge in 1989
The Span That Slipped in an Earthquake
sahneler: During the Loma Prieta earthquake, a section of the Bay Bridge fell.
A car drove into the gap, and the driver was killed.
The upper deck dropped onto the lower deck.
Shaking shifted a support tower.
Bolts holding the span sheared off.
The section slid off its support.
The bridge was closed for a month.
The eastern span was later replaced by a new seismic design.

baslik: The Tsunami That Rose Over Japan's Great Seawalls
sonuc: overtopped seawalls along Japan's coast
tetik: a tsunami far taller than the walls were built for
mekanizma: overtopping and scour of seawalls designed for smaller historical tsunamis
ders: Japan combined higher walls with evacuation planning and land-use changes
yanilgi: The walls didn't simply fail to exist. They were built for smaller tsunamis than this one.
tartisma: Some residents trusted the walls and didn't evacuate. Can protection make people less safe?
basliklar: Why the 2011 Tsunami Overtopped Japan's Seawalls
The Seawalls Built for a Smaller Wave
sahneler: After a magnitude nine earthquake, a tsunami struck Japan's coast.
Waves swept over seawalls and destroyed whole towns.
Many walls had been built for past tsunamis.
This one was far taller.
Water poured over the top and scoured the foundations.
Some residents trusted the walls and stayed.
Evacuation, not walls alone, saved the most lives.
Japan now combines walls with evacuation planning and land-use changes.

baslik: The City Built of Wood That Burned for Two Days
sonuc: burned through the heart of Chicago
tetik: a barn fire during a drought with strong winds
mekanizma: fire spread through wooden buildings and sidewalks, driven by wind in a dry season
ders: Chicago rebuilt with fire-resistant materials and stricter codes
yanilgi: The famous cow story was never proven. The real causes were drought, wind and a city built of wood.
tartisma: The fire destroyed the waterworks, removing the means to fight it. What single point of failure did Chicago have?
basliklar: Why the Great Chicago Fire Spread So Far
The Wooden City That Burned
How a Barn Fire Burned Down Chicago
soru: What was the single point of failure?
sahneler: A fire in a barn spread across the city of Chicago.
It burned for two days, destroying thousands of buildings.
The city was built largely of wood.
Even many sidewalks were wooden.
A drought had dried everything out.
Strong winds carried embers across the river.
The fire destroyed the waterworks.
Chicago rebuilt with fire-resistant materials and stricter codes.

baslik: The School Fire That Changed Fire Drills Forever
sonuc: burned with children trapped in the stairwell
tetik: a fire near the base of the main staircase
mekanizma: fire in a building with a wooden interior and exits that funnelled children into a narrow stairway
ders: schools adopted fire drills, outward-opening doors and fire-resistant construction
yanilgi: The doors weren't locked as often claimed. The narrow vestibule and crowding trapped the children.
tartisma: Many victims died metres from the exit. Is design or drilling the better protection?
basliklar: Why the Collinwood School Fire Was So Deadly
The Fire That Created School Fire Drills
sahneler: Fire broke out at an elementary school near Cleveland.
Children were trapped in the stairwell, and one hundred seventy two died.
The school had a wooden interior.
The fire started near the base of the stairs.
Children rushed toward a narrow exit.
They were crushed together in the vestibule.
Many died just metres from the door.
Schools then adopted fire drills and safer exits.

baslik: The Stadium Roof Tiles That Fell Before a Game
sonuc: dropped ceiling tiles into the seats
tetik: water getting behind the roof's ceiling tiles
mekanizma: waterlogged acoustic ceiling tiles detaching from the concrete dome
ders: the roof was repaired at great cost and the stadium was later demolished
yanilgi: The concrete dome itself stayed sound. The tiles fastened beneath it failed.
tartisma: Nobody was hurt because it happened before fans arrived. How often does timing hide a disaster?
basliklar: Why Ceiling Tiles Fell From the Kingdome
The Stadium That Dropped Its Ceiling
soru: How often does timing save us?
sahneler: Before a baseball game, heavy ceiling tiles fell from the Kingdome roof.
Suddenly, tiles crashed into the empty seats below.
Nobody was hurt, because fans hadn't arrived yet.
Water had been leaking into the roof.
It soaked the tiles and made them heavier.
They pulled away from the concrete dome.
The stadium closed for months of costly repairs.
It was later demolished and replaced.
